items.title: Map server-side workflow states and invariants
items.objective: Define valid states, transitions, actors, prerequisites, limits, and rollback before testing sequence abuse.
prerequisites: Owner-reviewed business rules and expected state transitions
Disposable accounts/objects, synthetic data, and explicit stopping/cleanup points
steps: Perform the normal workflow and record authoritative server states, actors, values, limits, and side effects
Create a clean synthetic control object or transaction
Change one sequence, state, value, identity, limit, timing, or channel condition
Verify authoritative outcome, restore/void test state, and compare with the documented invariant

examples.note: Use only synthetic records and zero-value or reversible transitions; stop before external or irreversible effects.

items.manipulate: One workflow sequence, state, numeric value, identity, limit, timing, callback, or channel at a time
items.secure_behavior: The server enforces documented business invariants, actor/state prerequisites, trusted calculations, usage limits, idempotency, and auditable transitions at the authoritative commit point.
items.vulnerable_behavior: a material workflow has no enforceable server-side invariant or cannot be reconciled with owner policy
items.validation: Confirm committed authoritative state or ledger effect and the violated owner-approved invariant; UI differences, accepted responses, or theoretical scaling alone are insufficient.
false_positives: UI steps do not always correspond one-to-one with server states
asynchronous intermediate states can be intentionally visible
items.impact: A confirmed business-logic flaw can cause financial loss, free goods/services, stored-value abuse, workflow/approval bypass, inventory denial, entitlement theft, fraud, spam, or regulatory harm.
evidence: Normal and modified workflow requests
